I like VRChat home, my quest friend says it has a nice mirror, and when too many people crowd the mirror it's time to go somewhere else. I do agree that the pens there suck, but again, motivation to not accidentally spend a session in one world.

The main reason I keep VRChat home as my home world is I like to see what they're promoting any given week. If they had a poster that could be syndicated via a remote image, I'd probably change up my home world.

For the hub,I think it's good for other users to make the more interesting worlds, why try and complete with your own users?

I think it's fine for VRChat to provide a robot and unimpressive world or two.

You could always set your home world to one of spookality

details:
As VRChat has grown, many things have evolved regarding how worlds are made, how they look, how many people can fit in them performantly, what things can be inside them, etc.

However, the VRChat Home and VRChat Hub have not seen significant updates in FOUR YEARS. They show their age, with an outdated visual style, lackluster features, and often low playercount.

In specific, as of writing, the VRChat Hub - the world which was intended to be the MAIN SOCIALUZING STARTING POINT for VRChat - only has 9 people in it across ALL instance, with only one in a public lobby. It can only hold up to 8 people, and looks horrendous. 

I believe the following should be the focuses of this world:

**Home** - An inviting, small-scale space to start off the game: One with a comforting, cozy atmosphere, features for just chilling alone or with one or two other friends, and one that feels like a proper starting space for VRChat. This should be stripped back of discovery and curation features, such as featured world portals, to make a world that is unobtrusive and welcoming.

**Hub** - A lively, large-scale space for socializing and meeting new people. This should include features that make people want to talk to others, like games, multiple, conversation areas, activities, important vistas and views, exploration, etc. This can be used to promote the community, featured content from the community, and the like so players can continue to explore VRChat. This space should be constantly updatable with new content and intriguing new features, such as examples of how to use new avatar or world creation content.

Things I would love to see in an updated Home & Hub:

Home:

- Video Player

- Updated Pens

- "Cozier" Atmosphere

- One or two lounging areas

- Nicer skybox/view

- More configurable mirror

- Permanent Hub portal

- Simple, small layout

- Potential outside area, inside area, and dark area

Hub 

- Performance Space

- Avatar Testing Area (with stands for all public avatars)

- Various hangout areas with varying sizes, aesthetics, etc.

- Game areas to engage in play with other players

- Consistently updated featured world portals (perhaps via string loading)?

- Nicer overviews and looks (not just a skybox, potentially a walking trail?).

- Potentially? a "tutorial" walking path that shows different aspects of the game

- More prominent featuring of community content (showing off events, dioramas of groups, etc.)

- Interactive displays & toys to show what is possible with avatar or world creation.

This is just a basic list of what I feel is missing, but could be more as time goes on. The point is that these worlds are woefully under-equipped for the current state of the game. They need much more:

- Engaging content

- Attractive visuals

- Distinctive spaces

- Thorough feature sets

To actually be flagship worlds for the platform. I really believe in the idea of official VRChat worlds, but think they are not currently at a point they should be at for their purposes.
title: New VRChat Home & Hub
